lines: {victim} came to us shaking. Why did you hit them, {player}?
Stop right there, {player}. {victim} says you struck them.
We heard what happened to {victim}. You should explain yourself.
{victim} ran for help before you found another reason to swing. Talk.
Do not walk past me like nothing happened. {victim} is frightened because of you.
Someone with less nerve than you still had enough courage to ask for help.
This village may look quiet, but we notice when one of us is hurt.
{victim} says your hand landed first. I want to hear why.
You have a moment to make this sound less ugly than it looks.
<shake>{player}</shake>, answer carefully. The whole village is listening now.

options.label: Apologize
responses: Then keep your hands down. I will tell {victim} you owned the harm.
An apology is a start. Let it be the last time {victim} has to run from you.
Good. Words are cheaper than trust, but they are better than another bruise.
I will pass that on. Do not make {victim} regret believing you.
Fine. I hear you. Now prove it by leaving them in peace.
{victim} deserves more than words, but words are where repair begins.
That is the right answer. Make sure your actions follow it.
I will not call this settled, but I will call it a start.
Apologizing does not erase it. It does give you a chance not to become worse.
<pulse>Good.</pulse> Let the next thing this village remembers be restraint.

options.label: It was an accident
responses: Accidents still leave people scared. Watch your reach around us.
Maybe. But {victim} believed it enough to run for help.
Then be more careful. The village will remember whether this becomes a pattern.
An accident is still your responsibility when someone else gets hurt.
I will accept that for now, but careless hands are still dangerous hands.
{victim} did not feel like an accident when they came to us.
Then slow down before your mistakes start looking like choices.
Fine. But if it happens again, no one will care what you meant.
You may not have meant harm, but harm still arrived.
Be careful, {player}. Around here, <wavy>accidents</wavy> have a way of becoming reputations.

options.label: Refuse to explain
responses: Then you have chosen the hard answer.
No explanation, no trust.
Silence after a hit is still an answer.
If you will not speak for yourself, we will believe {victim}.
That tells me enough.
You hurt someone and now offer nothing. Do not expect patience.
A closed mouth does not make the bruise disappear.
Fine. The village can live without your excuse.
Then we settle this without your side of the story.
<shake>Wrong choice.</shake>

options.label: Threaten them
responses: You do not get another warning.
Threaten one of us and you answer to more than one.
That was the wrong thing to say in a village that listens.
So that is who you are when someone asks a fair question.
You came close to making this worse. Then you stepped all the way in.
You should have apologized. Instead, you made yourself a danger.
Say another word like that and you will wish you had stayed silent.
The village heard you. That was your last mistake here.
You threaten the frightened and call it strength. Pathetic.
<shake><color:red>Enough.</color></shake>

leave_option.label: Leave
leave_option.response: Walk away if you want. <pulse>{victim}</pulse> will still remember who made them run.
